entities.name: Albi Cathedral
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Albi Cathedral (Cathédrale Sainte-Cécile d'Albi), begun in 1282 and built over 200 years in southern France's Languedoc region, is the world's largest brick cathedral and a fortified church deliberately designed as a military monument — its walls are 1.5 meters thick, its windows minimal, and its overall form resembles a fortress rather than a church. The cathedral's construction followed the Albigensian Crusade (1209-1229), which the Pope launched to exterminate the Cathar heresy; its architectural fortification embodies the Catholic Church's determination to demonstrate power over the region that had harbored heretics.

The Cathars, a Gnostic dualist sect particularly strong in the Languedoc, had been declared heretical by Pope Innocent III, who launched the Albigensian Crusade in 1209 to destroy them. The Crusade's culminating massacre at Béziers (1209), where 20,000 people were killed including Catholics (the Papal legate reportedly said 'Kill them all, God will know His own'), demonstrated the crusade's total war character. Albi, the region's center, gave the heretics their name — Albigenses.

The cathedral's interior contains an extraordinary contrast to the austere exterior: the greatest Gothic painted ceiling in the world (flamboyant Gothic paintings covering the entire vault, 1505-1512), an ornate rood screen (1500), and a 15th-century polychrome Last Judgment painting at the west end covering 200 m². The Toulouse-Lautrec Museum, housed in the adjacent Episcopal Palace, makes Albi a dual monument to medieval ecclesiastical power and 19th-century bohemian art. The cathedral's fortified form has been called the most terrifying building of the French Middle Ages.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Albi Cathedral — the world's largest brick building and a fortified monument to the Albigensian Crusade — is the most architecturally explicit embodiment of medieval Catholic power over heresy, its military exterior encoding the violence used to establish religious conformity.
